was: Apache-Sitgreaves NF (Big Lake Recreation Area), White Mountains ~9,000 ft. Largest Big Lake campground: 165 sites in six loops (incl. double and QUAD/group units), no hookups. Adjacent to 450-acre Big Lake (top AZ trout fishing). Mostly reservable online, some FCFS booked in person; open ~mid-May to mid-Sep, flush toilets/showers/potable water/camp store. --Claude

was: Prescott NF campground ~10 mi east of Dewey off Cherry Rd (dirt, passenger-car OK except in wet weather). 11 sites, first-come first-served, vault toilet, no drinking water; RVs to ~40 ft per listings though the access road is tight for big rigs. Flanked by seasonal Hackberry Wash (no perennial water). --Claude

was: Apache-Sitgreaves NF (Alpine RD), one of the East Fork Black River Recreation Area campgrounds ~13 mi from Alpine via graveled FR 249/FR 276. ~10 sites, concessionaire-operated, first-come first-served (not reservable), vault toilet, no potable water; East Fork of the Black River runs ~50 yds south. Sites are small and only some fit larger rigs. Open roughly mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

was: Coronado NF (Douglas RD), Chiricahua Mountains high country (~8,400 ft) reached via gravel FR 42/42D (2WD passable, high-clearance recommended). 21 single-family sites + 1 group, first-come first-served, drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups. RV/trailer max 22 ft (borderline for a 23-ft rig). Open ~Apr 1-Oct 31; area burned in the 2011 Horseshoe 2 Fire so canopy is thin. --Claude

Shaded Engelmann spruce/Douglas-fir grove; vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. Listed max RV 22 ft (over 22 ft not recommended due to Swift Trail switchbacks) — borderline for a 23-ft rig. Open ~Apr 15-Nov 14; AZ 366 gated closed in winter. --Claude

was: Forest Service campground at Stockton Pass (~5,700 ft) on paved AZ 266, about 17 mi south of Safford, Coronado NF Safford Ranger District. 7 individual first-come, first-served sites plus one reservable group site (recreation.gov); vault toilets, pedestal grills/fire rings, no potable water, no hookups; black-bear area. Listed max RV 22 ft, but reached via a normal through-highway (no switchbacks) and a 25-ft rig was reported firsthand, so a 23-ft rig fits. --Claude

Three primitive drive-in sites (tent/RV) with picnic tables, steel fire rings, and a vault toilet plus a 10-vehicle day-use lot; no water, no hookups. Reached via SR-85 to Woods Rd then ~5 mi graded desert dirt (high-clearance 2WD suitable). First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude

was: Coronado NF campground on Mt Graham's Swift Trail (AZ-366), ~6,770 ft in ponderosa pine and Gambel oak. 19 individual sites, first-come first-served; no hookups. RVs to 22 ft recommended - the AZ-366 switchbacks make longer rigs difficult (borderline for a 23-ft rig). Open year-round, weather permitting. --Claude

Reached via graded Aravaipa/Klondyke Rd then 0.75 mi on Fourmile Canyon Rd. --Claude

Reached via graded FR-249 then FR-276. --Claude

Often free off-peak. Some highway road noise. --Claude

Open May 1-Sep 30. --Claude

Reservable through Pima County for the main season with H-loop kept first-come, first-served; closed in high summer. --Claude

Some limited availability during the spring fair. --Claude

was: City of Winslow park on Clear Creek Reservoir ~5 mi SE of town (AZ 87 to AZ 99). Small campground, upper and lower areas, sites to ~40 ft; potable water, vault toilets, picnic tables, no hookups. First-come first-served (self-pay station), open year-round. --Claude

was: Verde Valley fairgrounds (800 E Cherry St, Cottonwood), operated by the nonprofit Verde Valley Fair Association; runs a year-round public RV camping area (open to all, not event-only). ~35 rigs; a few 30/50-amp electric sites plus dry camping, water fill and free dump station, no showers/full hookups. Big-rig/pull-through, RVs to ~40 ft. 14-day limit, first-come first-served. Confirmed operating (reviews through Jan 2026). --Claude

Open ~1st weekend of April through 1st weekend of October, Thu-Mon nights only; max stay 3 days. --Claude

was: Mohave County park on the Colorado River just below Davis Dam near Bullhead City; ~171 tent/RV sites along roughly 2 mi of developed shoreline, many full-hookup plus dry sites; restrooms with showers, dump/water fill, store, laundry, boat launch, swim beach, dog park. Graded-gravel pull-through and back-in full-hookup sites (30/50-amp electric, water, sewer), RVs to ~50 ft; on-site laundry, WiFi; no showers/restrooms; tents not permitted. No age restriction; ~half of sites held for first-come, first-served, other half reservable. --Claude

No hookups, one vault/porta-toilet, no water; some large potholes but level and RV-passable (reviewers pulled in 25-42 ft rigs, dirt access off SR-186). First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude

was: CAL FIRE demonstration state forest (Cobb/Middletown). Calso Camp is the forest's only non-group campground: 14 rustic sites, first-come first-served, self-issue camping permit from CAL FIRE; no hookups, no dump, no running water (bring your own), vault/pit toilets. Small trailers/RVs allowed if they fit the site. --Claude

was: Anza-Borrego Desert State Park, at the mouth of Bow Willow Canyon off County Hwy S-2 in the south of the park. 16 primitive drive-in sites, first-come first-served (no reservations); potable water, picnic tables, fire rings, shade ramadas, vault toilets, no hookups.
